human_name: HLA-B class-I locus (most polymorphic HLA gene, gene-conversion-prone)

GRCh38.note: HLA-B gene body on PGF reference haplotype; HLA-B and HLA-C are tightly linked (~70 kb apart) in the class-I tail of the MHC

architecture_note: HLA-B is the most polymorphic human gene by allele count. Like HLA-A/C, single-copy per haplotype but sits in the complex_mosaic MHC class-I sub-region. Pragmatic complex_mosaic tag per Norman 2017 / segdup_class_taxonomy.md.

exon_2.note: Hyperpolymorphic — primary allele-discrimination region. See IPD-IMGT/HLA for PSVs (CC-BY-ND, no inline copy).

exon_3.note: Hyperpolymorphic. Exon 2+3 carry the bulk of HLA-B coding diversity. HLA-B*57:01, B*15:02 etc. are defined primarily by exon 2/3 PSVs.

diagnostic_features.snp_density_note: HLA-B has >11000 distinct alleles (IPD-IMGT/HLA Release 3.55+, 2024) — the highest of any human gene. Per-position diversity in exons 2/3 prevents single-reference mapping.

ipd_imgt_reference.use: Resolve allele-specific PSVs and reference sequences via API

gene_conversion_evidence.note: Inter-allelic gene conversion at HLA-B is documented (Parham 1989; Chen 2007); HLA-B↔HLA-C cross-locus conversion also reported.

diagnostic_features.clinical_associations_note: HLA-B*57:01 (abacavir hypersensitivity), B*15:02 (carbamazepine SJS/TEN), B*27 (ankylosing spondylitis), B*51 (Behçet). Allele-level resolution is clinically required.

primary.note: Mirrors HLA-A strategy. HLA-B reads cross-map heavily to HLA-C (~70 kb downstream, ~88 % nt identity in coding region).

primary_sources.note: Norman PJ et al., Genome Res — 95 MHC haplotypes
Horton R et al., Immunogenetics — MHC Haplotype Project
Robinson J et al., maintainers; CC-BY-ND, external reference only

provenance.license_note: IPD-IMGT/HLA sequences/PSV lists are CC-BY-ND and NOT embedded in this catalog.
